newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran seeks world aid for quake victims.
newsitem.headline: Iran seeks world aid for quake victims.

text.p: Iran on Tuesday appealed for international aid for victims of an earthquake which devastated a mountainous region in its rugged northwest killing nearly 1,000 people.

The head of the United Nations Information Centre in Tehran, Iftikhar Ali, told Reuters: "Today we received Iran's request and the U.N. coordinator briefed ambassadors of donor countries, mostly European states, about the situation in the field."
The appeal came as Iran announced the deaths of four people on a relief flight to the stricken region who were killed when their light aircraft crashed in bad weather on Monday night.

Rescue teams battled knee-deep snow, freezing temperatures and marauding wolves in the search for more victims of Friday's quake that killed at least 965 people, injured 2,600 and left 36,000 homeless in Ardabil province near the Caspian Sea.

Some 60,000 people were affected by the earthquake which completely destroyed 20 villages and damaged 80 others in the agricultural province, which is inhabited mainly by Iran's Azeri minority, the U.N. said in a statement.
Heavy damage was also caused to roads, power lines, water supplies, schools and rural clinics. Some 30,000 head of livestock perished in the quake, which measured 5.5 on the Richter scale.
A second quake on Sunday was registered at 5.2 on the Richter scale and 500 aftershocks were recorded.
Search teams on Tuesday found the wreckage of the crashed plane and took the bodies of the four crew to a morgue, the official news agency IRNA said.
Iranian reporters said President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani had been due to fly to the quake zone on Tuesday to meet survivors and oversee relief operations but postponed his trip.
Tehran radio said Ardabil was Iran's coldest region on Monday night with temperatures of minus six degrees Celsius (21 degrees Fahrenheit).
A Red Crescent spokesman told Reuters: "The search operation continues and we expect more casualties. The death toll is still 965 people, but we expect to dig out more bodies."
"The snow is making the job difficult and slow," he added.
IRNA said heavy snow started to fall on the region on Monday night seriously hampering relief operations and cutting off roads to some quake-stricken villages.
Iran's Interior Minister Ali Mohammad Besharati said most of the dead were killed in the first earthquake and there were no reports on casualties from the second quake.
Iranian media said units of the army and Revolutionary Guards joined about 5,000 relief workers already involved in rescue operations.
The Red Crescent said more than 8,700 tents, 21,800 blankets, 15,300 heaters and lanterns, and 80 tonnes of bread had been distributed to victims.
It said Switzerland, Britain, Japan and some international relief organisations had offered aid. Saudi Arabia announced on Monday it was sending two plane loads of relief supplies.
Earthquakes hit Iran regularly. The worst recorded one, measuring 7.3 on the Richter scale, killed 35,000 people near the Caspian coast in 1990.
